review_notes: I read the whole file and checked the helper API in PermutationQuotient.lean (pointStabilizerCoreQuotientAction_mk_smul). I also searched the repo for uses of the private lemmas. Other candidates were rejected as not repeated, as too short, or as outside this rubric. The conjugation calculations in involution_eq_u_of_centralized and not_twoRankAtLeastTwo_normalizer differ in substance. The mem_stabilizer unfolding in lemma103_pointStabilizerCore_le_pairStabilizer is short. The private lemma103_quotient_action_twoPretransitive is unused and duplicates the htwoBar step of lemma_10_3, but it is dead code rather than repeated proof machinery. I did not compile any replacement, so the rewrites below are sketches. The first one is a local change and should be low-risk, but the elaboration of the instance arguments is the main uncertainty.

findings.excerpt: have hrepresentative : uBar • omega = uStar • omega := by
findings.problem: The same 6-line argument that the quotient action of the class of uStar agrees with the normalizer action of uStar is proved twice, once for alpha and once for an arbitrary omega. Each copy has a delicate `@pointStabilizerCoreQuotientAction_mk_smul N Omega _ (lemma103NormalizerAction M P) hcoreNormal ...` call plus a `change @SMul.smul ...` that exposes the instance. The alpha copy is just the omega copy specialised to omega = alpha. The same instance-juggling pattern also appears elsewhere in the repo (Section11Lemma115QuotientLift.lean), so each copy is a maintenance hazard.
findings.proposed_change: Prove the statement once, before huAlpha, in universally quantified form: `have hrep : ∀ omega : Omega, uBar • omega = uStar • omega := by intro omega; have hmk := @pointStabilizerCoreQuotientAction_mk_smul N Omega _ (lemma103NormalizerAction M P) hcoreNormal uStar omega; change @SMul.smul Nbar Omega (@pointStabilizerCoreQuotientAction N Omega _ (lemma103NormalizerAction M P) hcoreNormal).toSMul (QuotientGroup.mk uStar) omega = uStar • omega; exact hmk`. Then huAlpha begins `rw [hrep alpha]; apply Subtype.ext; ...` and huUnique uses `(hrep omega).symm.trans homega`. For a more reusable fix, add a lemma that reduces fixing by the class to fixing by the representative: `(QuotientGroup.mk g : G ⧸ pointStabilizerCore G Omega) • omega = omega ↔ g • omega = omega`. Such a lemma would belong in PermutationQuotient.lean and the Lemma 11.5 copies could use it too.
findings.benefit: This removes about 10 duplicated lines of instance-sensitive proof. The one place the quotient and normalizer actions are identified becomes a single named fact, and the proofs of huAlpha and huUnique shrink to the real mathematics: fixed points of u in the ambient coset space.

findings.excerpt: have huCentP : d83.u ∈ Subgroup.centralizer (P : Set X) := by
findings.problem: Three proofs repeat the argument that P, being contained in V = D ∩ C(t), lies in D ∩ C(u). Each unfolds `d.choice.P_le_V hpP`, uses `change` to expose `(M ⊓ rightConjugate M t) ⊓ centralizer {t}`, and rewrites with `d83.centralizer_eq`. This occurs at 414-418, 534-538 and 660-664. Two of the proofs, not_twoRankAtLeastTwo_normalizer and lemma_10_3, then also repeat the follow-on steps: u centralizes P, hence u ∈ N_X(P) via `centralizer_le_normalizer`, hence the subtype involution uN/uStar (lines 411-422 and 665-672). If the definition of peterfalviV or of the `centralizer_eq` field changes, all three places need the same `change` fix.
findings.proposed_change: Add two lemmas next to the others, under the same hypotheses as the callers. First, `Lemma101Conclusion.P_le_inf_centralizer_u (d) (d83 : Lemma83Data M t) : d.choice.P ≤ (M ⊓ rightConjugate M t) ⊓ Subgroup.centralizer ({d83.u} : Set X)`. Its proof is the existing 5-line block: `intro p hpP; have hpV := d.choice.P_le_V hpP; change ... at hpV; rw [d83.centralizer_eq] at hpV; exact hpV`. Second, `Lemma101Conclusion.u_mem_normalizer (d) (d83) : d83.u ∈ lemma103NStar d.choice.P`. Its proof gets centralization from `(d.P_le_inf_centralizer_u d83 hpP).2` via `Subgroup.mem_centralizer_singleton_iff`, and then applies `centralizer_le_normalizer`. Then lemma103_three_le_omega becomes `hM.three_le_fixedPoints_of_le_lemma83V ht htM d83 (fun p hp => d.P_le_inf_centralizer_u d83 hp)`. In not_twoRankAtLeastTwo_normalizer and lemma_10_3, huCentP/huN are replaced by one call, with `uN`/`uStar := ⟨d83.u, d.u_mem_normalizer d83⟩`.
findings.benefit: The Lemma 10.1 to Lemma 8.3 link, that P fixes u and so u normalizes P, is stated and proved once under a descriptive name. The three callers lose about 25 lines of `change`/`rw` boilerplate, and the 2-rank argument and the main theorem read as direct uses of the fact that P ≤ C(u).
